section_summary: This section concerns efforts to bring Japanese unions into a new non-Communist international labor federation, including plans for a five-member delegation to its London meeting. It also contains a union petition about politically motivated dismissals, Soviet allegations of repression of Japanese workers, MacArthur’s response, and a 1947 inquiry into conditions among Hokkaido coal miners.

subfiles.title: Memorandum recommending international contacts for non-Communist Japanese unions
subfiles.about: Recommends allowing invited non-Communist Japanese unionists to attend meetings of a new international labor body.
subfiles.summary: Argues that international contacts would strengthen Japanese non-Communist labor leaders despite SCAP’s concerns about Communist travel.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable to General MacArthur on Japanese participation in the new international trade union federation
subfiles.about: Seeks State Department approval for a cable favoring Japanese union participation.
subfiles.summary: Explains Labor Department support, the expected benefits, and MacArthur’s earlier reluctance to distinguish between Communist and non-Communist unions.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram to SCAP on Japanese delegates to the new trade union federation
subfiles.about: Urges permission for invited non-Communist Japanese union representatives to attend the London founding convention.
subfiles.summary: Describes the new federation’s formation and gives four reasons for Japanese attendance: countering WFTU claims in Asia, strengthening anti-Communist unions, raising their prestige, and encouraging unity.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 614 concerning a ministry workers’ union petition
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a petition protesting dismissals at the Ministry of International Trade and Industry.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the union’s complaint and supporting material about a personnel reduction.

subfiles.title: Petition from Ministry of International Trade and Industry Workers’ Labour Union
subfiles.about: Requests investigation and cancellation of allegedly political dismissals of ministry employees.
subfiles.summary: Claims the dismissals targeted Communists and union officers and violated constitutional, labor, and public service protections.

subfiles.title: List of dismissed ministry personnel and union affiliations
subfiles.from: Ministry of International Trade and Industry Workers’ Labour Union
subfiles.about: Lists dismissed employees, ages, offices, political affiliations, and union roles.
subfiles.summary: The roster identifies workers across ministry bureaus and the Resources Agency, many labeled Communist or described as current or former union officers.

subfiles.title: Reported Japanese delegate to the National CIO convention
subfiles.about: Discusses reports that Eiichi Ochiai was chosen to attend the CIO convention.
subfiles.summary: Notes uncertainty about a CIO invitation and defers action until Michael Ross consults James Carey.

subfiles.title: Invitations for Japanese trade unionists to attend meetings abroad
subfiles.about: Reports CIO discussions of invitations to London and reception of a possible Japanese delegate in Cleveland.
subfiles.summary: Ross plans to seek a broader London invitation; Carey says the CIO would welcome a Japanese visitor, so Sullivan recommends no SCAP action.

subfiles.title: Conversation with British Embassy official about Japanese invitations
subfiles.about: Records British TUC interest in inviting Japan’s new joint union council to London.
subfiles.summary: J. J. Watson reports that Vincent Tewson favors inclusion and may allow the council to defer payment of federation dues.

subfiles.title: Information on proposed Japanese labor delegation to London
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP Labor Division material on the proposed delegation.
subfiles.summary: Reports two documents from Robert T. Amis and a request for the delegates to stop in Washington on their return.

subfiles.title: Japanese delegates to London
subfiles.about: Explains how five Japanese unions chose delegates for the London conference.
subfiles.summary: The joint council selected five unions by ballot, and each chose a delegate and alternate. SCAP was arranging clearance and funding while seeking an invitation addressed to the council itself.

subfiles.title: Information for the preparatory committee on Japanese union representation
subfiles.to: Preparatory Committee of the new free trade union federation
subfiles.about: Describes the joint council’s membership, affiliates, delegates, and requested invitation.
subfiles.summary: Lists member unions and estimated memberships, discusses plans for a broader federation, names the five delegates and alternates, and asks that the invitation go to council secretary Asahi Okura.

subfiles.title: Japanese delegation to the free trade union meeting in London
subfiles.about: Reports that the British TUC invited five joint-council delegates and forwards biographies and an itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Suggests consulting Labor, AFL, and CIO officials about the delegation’s planned week in Washington.

subfiles.title: Personal history of Shozaburo Araki
subfiles.about: Records Araki’s addresses, education, and teachers’ union leadership.
subfiles.summary: Traces his rise through Osaka teachers’ unions to leadership of the Japan Teachers Union.

subfiles.title: Curriculum vitae of Yukitaka Haraguchi
subfiles.about: Records Haraguchi’s education and work in metal mining and union leadership.
subfiles.summary: Describes his Besshi mine employment and chairmanship of the metal mining workers’ federation.

subfiles.title: Curriculum vitae of Komakichi Matsuoka
subfiles.about: Summarizes Matsuoka’s long labor career, international travel, and public offices.
subfiles.summary: Lists union leadership, labor conference service, and later roles including legislator and federation president.

subfiles.title: Curriculum vitae of Etsuo Kato
subfiles.about: Records Kato’s railway employment and union leadership.
subfiles.summary: Describes his railway posts and repeated election as chairman of the National Railway Workers Union.

subfiles.title: Curriculum vitae of Chuso Moriguchi
subfiles.about: Records Moriguchi’s education, newspaper employment, and union work.
subfiles.summary: Traces his Mainichi employment and subsequent leadership of Tokyo unions and Zen Nichiro.

subfiles.title: Travel itinerary for five Japanese trade union representatives
subfiles.about: Schedules travel to London and a Washington stopover for five delegates.
subfiles.summary: Gives flights through Minneapolis and New York, meeting dates, return travel, and per-passenger cost.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese unions and the Peiping trade union conference
subfiles.about: Relays a Pravda/TASS report of a Japanese trade union conference meeting on November 27.
subfiles.summary: Reports the announced meeting and asks that the information be passed to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Reply to Soviet statement in the Far Eastern Commission on labor
subfiles.about: Submits a draft reply to Soviet labor allegations and discusses the WFTU Peiping meeting.
subfiles.summary: Recommends releasing the reply if the Soviet statement becomes public and discusses whether to circulate the Peiping manifesto.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 895 transmitting Soviet letter on Japanese trade unions
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits the Soviet member’s letter to MacArthur and MacArthur’s public statement.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Soviet charges of police repression and political dismissals, characterizes the letter as a diversion from the Japanese repatriation issue, and lists two enclosures.

subfiles.title: Soviet letter on anti-democratic measures toward Japanese trade unions
subfiles.about: Alleges that Japanese government and occupation policies repress unions and democratic activity.
subfiles.summary: The letter cites police actions, arrests, dismissals, restrictions on political activity, and proposed laws as violations of the Potsdam Declaration and Far Eastern Commission policy. It asks MacArthur to require repeal of restrictions, an end to repression, and reinstatement of dismissed workers and teachers.

subfiles.title: General MacArthur accepts council recommendation
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces an effort to investigate missing Japanese prisoners and rejects Soviet allegations.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur calls for neutral help in tracing prisoners and describes the Soviet labor charges as a diversion.

subfiles.title: War Department inquiry into Hokkaido coal-miner conditions
subfiles.about: Requests verification of reports of coercion and abuse among Hokkaido coal miners.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether miners were held under a prison-cell system and employers used force to prevent union organizing.
